analysis: Every changed file in this batch is test or golden data: a new Swift placement check (GemmaTensorParallelChecks.swift), golden plan hashes in expected.json, and the gemma-4-26b-8bit golden layout. No production code, authn/authz, crypto, secret handling or network paths are touched, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 or T-041. The check file reads only local retained fixture files (StageMetadataChecks/Inputs), builds synthetic Macs and links, and makes no network or GPU calls. It never touches the Secure Enclave, attestation, tokens or prompts. The golden layout for gemma-4-26b-8bit now lists tensor_parallel_v1 in generationModes and adds a tensorParallel block. That block has family.choice fastest_v1, routedExperts and ranks [2]. The expected.json plan hashes change only for the gemma entries, and they are pipeline_v1 hashes, which is consistent with the layout changes. The golden layouts carry only numeric byte counts, shapes and a plan name, with no secrets. The check asserts that a Gemma pair is placed in tensor parallel only where the planner predicts it faster, and that a kept pipeline, an unmeasured link on an automatic replacement, or a forced mode behaves as expected. These are performance placement policy checks, not security controls. Remaining integration questions are outside the supplied evidence. They concern the production planner, protocol and worker code (ClusterTensorParallelChoice.fastest, the sealed_all_gather_sum_v1 reduction keying and the stage-metadata decoders). Those files must be reviewed separately for any authentication, sealing or resource-bound change that enabling tensor parallel by default for Gemma might introduce. This batch alone shows none.
